How many cordys be þer of dyscant? be þer ix. Whych ix? a vnison de iijde v vj viij x xij xiij xv. How many be perfyght & how many be imperfyght? v be perfyght & iiij be imperfyght ... Whan thow art wyt hym in syght thow art viij from hym. An vnison ys viij benethe in syght. A iijde ys a vj benethe in syght
(fol. 63v) First figuracyon of ... thes ben þe substans of fyguracyon vsyd in thyse dayes
Then be þer iiij mesures þat ys for to say perfyte of the moore and perfyte of the lesse
Then be þer iij maner of prykkes þat ys to say a prykke of perfeccyon a prykke of dyuysyon a prykke of reduccyon a

history.provenance: Fols. 2r-62v written by Alex. Capel . Written inside the initial on fol. 2 in the same ink is ‘alex. Capel’, inside that on fol. 29v ‘alex’, and at the end of book I (fol. 39) ‘quod Alex.’

At fol. 61v in a different hand from that of the text is ‘Hic finit colni sentencia nobilis ensis quod Thomas Pett ’ (perhaps the Thomas Pett who was Keeper of the Chest with Four Keys at Oxford in 1452, cf. Emden Biographical Register III, p.1471).

John Hychcoke . ‘Iste liber constat domino Johanni Hychecoke emtus a domino Iohanne Aschby bachulario artium in aula vitrea (Glasen Hall) commorante et predictus dominus J. H. in aula beate Marie pro ij s. vj d.’ (fol. 61v). For Hychecok, admitted B.A. at Oxford 1450 cf. Emden op. cit. II. p.929; since he is not styled magister he presumably acquired the book before 1454; his name is also on fol. 1r.
'Quod Thomas Ganne bonus et non prauus', fol. 64v, see Emden II.741
On fol. 1r in a 15th cent. hand is a list of sums paid for items including candles, paper, ink and battels headed by the name ‘Hungerford’.

, Davies-Cooke family of Gwysaney, Llanerch and Owston (Gwysaney library), MS. 16 (HMC Sixth Report App. p. 419); apparently identifiable as 41 ('Old divinity, Latin') and 40 in the catalogues of 1740 and 1778 ('The Gywsaney manuscripts', National Library of Wales Journal 7/4 (1952) 326-343 at 329-30.).
